yuna: quick heads-up from int6 bringup: tempesta-v2-int6 shows two locale-y regressions in the multiorient subtitle smoke — (1) Japanese vertical + ruby (furigana) lines have punctuation and ruby anchors glued to main ideographs causing misaligned furigana, (2) Arabic math/mixed RTL lines show brace/curly-brace mirroring flips in rendered output. minimal repro below.
omar: can you drop the exact command and a tiny failing snippet?
yuna: running: `rrun eval --model=tempesta-v2-int6 --suite=multiorient_subs --subset=ja_vertical_ruby,arabic_math_rtl --shards=fast --jobs=6 --log-token-ids`

summary (fast shard):
```
ja_vertical_ruby: RUBY-anchor mismatch baseline=0 -> int6=34/200 failures, BLEU delta -4.8
arabic_math_rtl: brace-mirror flips baseline=0 -> int6=17/200
en_subs: unchanged
```

yuna: minimal ja example input (vertical with ruby markup):
`漢字(かんじ)＼ruby:かんじ`  # simplified repro line
baseline detok tokens: ["(","漢字",")","ruby:かんじ"]
int6 detok tokens:   ["(漢字)","ruby:かんじ"]  # bracket glued to ideograph -> ruby anchor misaligns

omar: and arabic case?
yuna: arabic input: `س = { x | x \u2066> 0 }` (curly braces around set)
baseline render: braces keep their visual mirrored shape in RTL context
int6 render: braces appear inverted/mirrored pair swapped in visual layout causing math to read incorrectly

sasha: do token ids differ between good/bad? if tokenizer changed we'd expect id diffs.
yuna: token ids are identical in failing examples. added `--log-detok --log-token-ids` and saw same ids but different rendered layout. snippet: `token_ids=[310,4412,19,78]` for both, but render differs.

vik: packaging notes for int6: per-head quant-scale folding, new kvcache compaction heuristic, swapped to packed-attn-quant kernels. suspect compaction timing + quant noise nudges hidden states -> shaping/layout differences downstream.

ben: I ran an A/B with `--no-kvcache-compaction --force-stable-quant`: ja_vertical_ruby failures drop to 3/200 and arabic flips -> 0/200. so compaction + quant folding looks implicated.
sasha: that matches other multiorient anomalies. even tiny attention shifts on punctuation tokens can change whether we emit ZWJ/ZWSP or how the bidi pass classifies bracket pairs. identical ids + different render => downstream shaping/layout change.
yuna: created a tiny repro file at `/evals/smoke/multiorient/ja_ar_brace_repro_1777778888.txt` and uploaded sample renders to `/evals/smoke/renders/1777778888/` for UX.

vik: next steps: 1) add a locale-aware small smoke to CI that runs int6 builds on a 50-sample multiorient shard and asserts no ruby-anchor glue or RTL-brace flips; 2) gate aggressive kvcache compaction for mixed-script/mixed-direction sequences; 3) add a `quant-stability` build flag to disable aggressive per-head folding for early canaries; 4) run a kernel-only revert (packed-attn-quant -> packed-attn) to confirm kernel interaction.

ben: filing BR-1517 with logs + hidden-state diffs and a small bisect plan. will tag eng-runtime, eng-ml, and ux.

ci-bot: canary job queued: tempesta-int6-multiorient-canary #86021 (compaction=false)
sasha: thanks team. happy to pair on the hidden-state diff harness (vik/ben), let's land the CI smoke first so this gets caught early. :eyes:
